questions.q: In Snowflake, who or what does a GRANT statement target?
options: A role — privileges are granted to roles, then roles are granted to users
The account as a whole, with no per-object control
A user directly, bypassing roles entirely
Only warehouses, never databases or tables
questions.explain: Snowflake grants privileges to roles, not users directly. Users get access by being granted the role — revoking the role removes every privilege that came with it in one step.

questions.q: What does the USAGE privilege on a warehouse, database, or schema actually do?
options: Lets a role 'see through' to what's inside, without granting access to any data by itself
Deletes the object if unused for 24 hours
Nothing — USAGE is not a real Snowflake privilege
Immediately grants SELECT on every table inside it
questions.explain: USAGE lets a role reach into a warehouse, database, or schema, but a role still needs an object-level privilege like SELECT to actually read data once it's inside.

questions.q: A role has SELECT on a table but no USAGE grant on that table's database or schema. What happens when it tries to query the table?
options: The query succeeds because SELECT overrides USAGE requirements
The query fails — the role can't reach the table without USAGE on the database and schema
The role gets read-only access to the entire database instead
Snowflake automatically grants USAGE the first time SELECT is used
questions.explain: USAGE and SELECT are layered — missing USAGE on the database or schema means the role can't reach the table at all, regardless of what table-level privileges it holds.

questions.q: What is a 'future grant' used for?
options: Granting a privilege that expires after 30 days
A grant that only takes effect after ACCOUNTADMIN approval
Scheduling a GRANT statement to run at a specific time in the future
Automatically applying a grant to objects that don't exist yet, so new tables in a schema inherit the same access
questions.explain: A future grant (e.g. GRANT SELECT ON FUTURE TABLES IN SCHEMA ...) applies automatically to objects created later, so new tables don't end up silently unreadable.

questions.q: Which command lets you audit exactly what privileges a role currently holds?
options: DESCRIBE ROLE <role>
EXPLAIN GRANTS <role>
SELECT * FROM ROLES
SHOW GRANTS TO ROLE <role>
questions.explain: SHOW GRANTS TO ROLE lists every privilege a role currently has — the fastest way to catch a role that's accumulated more access than its job needs.
